Einleitung p92a.text: Now, as a content in order to possess truth at all must be of this concrete nature, art demands the same concreteness, because a mere abstract universal has not in itself the vocation to advance to particularity and phenomenal manifestation and to unity with itself therein. If a true and therefore concrete content is to have corresponding to it a sensuous form and modelling, this sensuous form must, in the third place, be no less emphatically something individual, wholly concrete in itself, and one.

transcription.reason: Human transcription of two printed pages; the sentence boundaries, paragraph separation and source typography were checked directly on the scan.
transcription.original_text: Now, as a content in order to possess truth at all must be of this concrete nature, art demands the same concreteness, because a mere abstract universal has not in itself the vocation to advance to particularity and phenomenal manifestation and to unity with itself therein. If a true and therefore concrete content is to have corresponding to it a sensuous form and modelling, this sensuous form must, in the third place, be no less emphatically something individual, wholly concrete in itself, and one.

Einleitung p92a.alignment: Both full sentences follow the German truth of content, the reason for art’s demand, and the conditional necessity of individual concrete form. The opening as may read causally rather than as the German analogy, and one can suggest unity where Einzelnes more precisely means the singular; the German emphasis on drittens is not reproduced.

Einleitung p92a.alignment: I independently read German pp. 92–93 and Bosanquet pp. 135–136. Both complete sentences preserve the truth of content, causal reason and conditional necessity. As weakens the comparative connection and one may mean unity rather than singularity; the German emphasis on drittens is absent in English. The page and paragraph boundary is normalized.
